newsitem.title: USA: IBM launches two new System/390 servers.
newsitem.headline: IBM launches two new System/390 servers.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp. Tuesday unveiled its third generation of low-cost mainframes, which are almost twice as fast as current models, and said it may sell out of all it can make this year.

The two new families of System/390 network servers, or computers that manage a network, are designed to help large and medium-sized companies with their growth on the Internet as well as for the internal networks known as intranets.

"Customers have been enthusiastic about embracing the new server," said Ross Mauri, vice president of System 390 hardware development at IBM. He added that it was likely that IBM will be "sold out of what we can produce this year," based on the initial customer reaction.
"The feedback is phenomenal," Mauri said. "We have seen quite a bit of demand out there."

The two server lines are the System/390 parallel enterprise server Generation 3, which has double the capacity of previous S/390 CMOS servers, and the System/390 Multiprise 2000 line, designed specifically for businesses looking for an alternative to UNIX or Windows NT servers, it said.

Three years ago, IBM unveiled its lower-cost CMOS (complementary metal oxide semiconductor) technology as the future and gradually its big corporate users have been moving to the new systems, which are less expensive to make. But the CMOS systems were not as powerful as IBM's older bipolar line.
IBM executives said they believed there were several reasons fuelling the customer demand for the new models, which are almost twice as fast as currently available CMOS-based mainframes.

The new models are less expensive to operate, and depending on what models a company has now, they can use up to 90 percent to 95 percent less power, resulting in a big cost savings. The new mainframes also can take up to 90 percent to 95 percent less floor space, depending on the current systems installed.
Other factors fuelling the customer interest are new software links that connect the mainframes to the Internet and to UNIX-based systems.

IBM also unveiled a new version of its mainframe operating system, called OS/390 Release 2, which includes many features and Internet gateway connections that let corporations integrate some of the vast amounts of data in their mainframe databases with the Internet.
IBM declined to give any specifics about prices, saying that it tailored each offering to unique customer requirements.
